subject: Follow-up: EU data residency & deployment mode options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Simon Hansen <simon.hansen@nordbank.eu>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Follow-up from discovery call — EU residency needs

Thanks for the call this morning, Neha — quick recap from my side and a couple of clarifications so we can get procurement moving.

Highlights:
- Our legal/compliance team requires all customer data and logs to remain within the EU.
- We are evaluating three deployment modes: Hosted API (EU region), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in EU), and Private VPC/on-prem for full isolation.
- Latency target for our customer-facing assistant is 250ms p95.
- Expected steady-state traffic is ~50 req/s with spikes to 200 req/s during business hours.

Questions:
1) For Hosted API in the EU region, does Redwood guarantee that tokens and logs never leave the EU? If not, what controls exist to prevent cross-region routing?
2) If we choose Dedicated capacity, can we reserve capacity in a specific EU region and pin model versions?
3) For Private (VPC/on-prem), what is typical lead time and does Redwood provide an on-prem appliance or only VPC workflows?

I've looped in procurement (procurement@nordbank.eu) — they want a short note we can attach to the vendor assessment.

Cheers,
Simon
Simon Hansen
Head of AI Platforms, NordBank

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Simon Hansen <simon.hansen@nordbank.eu>
Cc: Thomas Berg <procurement@nordbank.eu>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up from discovery call — EU residency needs

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear recap and for looping procurement in. Below is a concise summary you can attach to your vendor pack, plus next steps.

Short answer summary (high-level):
- Hosted API (EU region): We offer hosted endpoints with EU-region tenancy. For most models, data and logs are stored in the EU. HOWEVER: for very large model loads or specific model variants, our smart routing can route to compatible replicas in other regions if EU capacity is temporarily saturated. We can disable cross-region fallback for customers that require strict residency.
- Dedicated capacity: Yes — you can reserve GPU pools in a specific EU region and pin model versions. Dedicated is the middle ground: predictable throughput and isolation at the compute layer, with customer data staying in-region.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full control. VPC/private control plane keeps metadata and logs in-customer-managed network; on-prem deployments are available for regulated customers. Typical timeline is longer (we estimate 6–12 weeks depending on SSO/KMS integrations and procurement).

Notes on controls we can provide:
- Residency SLA addendum: we can add a contract clause to prohibit cross-region routing and require EU-only storage.
- Key management: integrate with your KMS/HSM in the EU so customer-managed keys never leave the region.
- Audit logs: full delivery of audit logs to your SIEM in-region.

Immediate next steps I recommend:
1) Please fill the attached deployment_requirements.xlsx with: required features, throughput profile, compliance checklist items, and preferred timeline.
2) We can schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Aditya) to go through pinning, autoscaling behavior, and latency expectations.
3) If procurement prefers, I'll draft a short cover note (1 page) that you can attach to the vendor assessment.

I've also attached our data residency whitepaper for a short read.

Proposed times for technical deep-dive: Thu 12 Feb 10:00-11:00 CET or Fri 13 Feb 14:00-15:00 CET — does either work?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.inference
+1 415-555-0182

From: Simon Hansen <simon.hansen@nordbank.eu>

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up from discovery call — EU residency needs

Thanks Neha — that's very helpful. A few follow-ups:
- Procurement would prefer a clear statement that Hosted API (EU-region) will not route outside the EU. If that requires a contract addendum, fine — they'd like the language.
- Our security team leans toward Private VPC/on-prem for high-risk customer data. Can you confirm: is there an on-prem option where we can host the inference runtime entirely inside our network, or is the private option VPC-only with a Redwood-managed control plane?
- Timeline: 6–12 weeks is ok, but we need an estimate for a VPC-only vs fully on-prem deployment.

I'll get the deployment_requirements.xlsx back to you by EOD tomorrow.

Simon

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Simon Hansen <simon.hansen@nordbank.eu>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Thomas Berg <procurement@nordbank.eu>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up from discovery call — EU residency needs

Simon — great, thanks for the quick turn on the requirements spreadsheet. A couple of clarifications from our side and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need: 

1) Hosted API residency addendum: we can include a contract addendum that prohibits cross-region fallback and requires all token storage and logs to remain in the EU region. This is an addendum to our data processing agreement; Aditya, can you confirm the standard language and any limitations?

2) Private options: we support two flavors for strict-residency customers: 
   - Private VPC: customer-managed network with a private control plane; Redwood services run in the customer's cloud account/region. Typical delivery 6–8 weeks (SSO/KMS/config reqs).
   - On-prem inference: we do offer an on-prem package for very regulated customers. That involves an appliance/container bundle plus a local ops runbook. Typical delivery 8–12 weeks depending on customer's infra and procurement lead times.

3) Dedicated capacity: can be provisioned in a specific EU region and supports pinning model versions and reserve throughput. Good option if you want predictable performance faster than on-prem.

Next actions:
- I'll draft the residency addendum language and send an initial version to procurement (Thomas) by EOD Fri 13 Feb.
- Aditya will join the technical deep-dive (Thu 12 Feb 10:00 CET). Aditya, please bring details on: model pinning, autoscale thresholds, cross-region fallback controls, and KMS integrations.
- Simon / Thomas: please share the completed deployment_requirements.xlsx — that will let us size Dedicated estimates and give a more accurate on-prem timeline.

If you want, I can also provide a short comparison table (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for procurement.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
